ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p133/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p133/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p133/r1.claim: The Day destroys the world and raises people; Hell awaits the rebellious, every deed is registered, and their punishment is the natural result of what they did.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p133/r1.anchor: Each will face the deeds he had sent forward and each and every deed of his will be written in a register.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p144/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p144/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p144/r2.claim: Hell appears immediately after the upheaval as though it had lain in ambush; rebels get no time to prepare.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p144/r2.anchor: Hell will appear so suddenly as if it was lying in ambush

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p386/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p386/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p386/r1.claim: مرصادا is an intensive place noun: Hell watches those condemned to punishment.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p386/r1.anchor: مرصادا: مفعال من الرصد، ترصد من حقت عليه كلمة العذاب.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p386/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p386/r2.speaker: مقاتل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p386/r2.claim: Hell is a station for enemies and a passage for friends.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p386/r2.anchor: وقال مقاتل: مجلسا للأعداء وممرا للأولياء، ومفعال للمذكر

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p386/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p386/r3.speaker: الأزهري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p386/r3.claim: مرصاد is a place where an enemy is watched; al-Hasan says the Fire lets those with good deeds pass and detains the rest.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p386/r3.anchor: وقال الأزهري: المرصاد: المكان الذي يرصد فيه العدو.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p386/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p386/r4.speaker: أبو عمر، المنقري، ابن يعمر
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p386/r4.claim: They read أن جهنم with hamza fatḥa; the majority use kasra.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p386/r4.anchor: وقرأ أبو عمر والمنقري وابن يعمر: أن جهنم، يفتح الهمزة والجمهور: بكسرها

NAHHAS:v5p127/r6.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p127/r6.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v5p127/r6.claim: Hell watches for those who disobey God; mirṣād derives from raṣadtu, and is not feminine because it is not directly a verbal form.
NAHHAS:v5p127/r6.anchor: أي ترصد من عصى الله سبحانه وترك طاعته وقال الحسن لا يدخل أحد الجنة

NAHHAS:v5p127/r7.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p127/r7.speaker: الحسن
NAHHAS:v5p127/r7.claim: Al-Ḥasan says no one enters Paradise before passing over Hell.
NAHHAS:v5p127/r7.anchor: قال الحسن لا يدخل أحد الجنة حتى يرد النار

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p425#2/r12.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p425#2/r12.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p425#2/r12.claim: مرصادا means a place of watch, as in 89:14; Hasan, Qatada, and a sound hadith say everyone must cross Hell, with the rescued passing and the others falling.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p425#2/r12.anchor: ومرصادا: موضع الرصد، ومنه قوله تعالى: إن ربك لبالمرصاد [الفجر: 14]

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p425#2/r13.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p425#2/r13.speaker: الحسن بن أبي الحسن
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p425#2/r13.claim: Hasan says no one enters Paradise without crossing Hell; those with means of rescue are saved and the rest perish.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p425#2/r13.anchor: وقد روي عن الحسن بن أبي الحسن أنه قال: «لا يدخل أحد الجنة حتى يجوز على جهنم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p425#2/r14.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p425#2/r14.speaker: قتادة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p425#2/r14.claim: Qatada says there is no way to Paradise without crossing the Fire.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p425#2/r14.anchor: وقال قتادة: تعلمن أنه لا سبيل إلى الجنة حتى تقطع النار

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p425#2/r15.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p425#2/r15.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p425#2/r15.claim: A sound hadith describes the bridge over Hell, crossed by people who are either saved or cast down.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p425#2/r15.anchor: وفي الحديث الصحيح: «إن الصراط جسر ينصب على متن جهنم ثم يجوز عليه الناس فناج ومكردس»

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p425#2/r16.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p425#2/r16.speaker: بعض المتأولين
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p425#2/r16.claim: Some interpreters take مرصادا as an active noun meaning one who watches.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p425#2/r16.anchor: وقال بعض المتأولين: مرصادا مفعال بمعنى راصد

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p425#2/r17.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p425#2/r17.speaker: أبو معمر المنقري
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p425#2/r17.claim: Abu Maʿmar reads أن جهنم with an open hamza; most readers use kasra.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p425#2/r17.anchor: وقرأ أبو معمر المنقري: «أن جهنم» بفتح الألف والجمهور: على كسرها

JISHUMI:v10p7247#2/r8.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7247#2/r8.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7247#2/r8.claim: Mirsād is a watchpoint equipped to observe something expected to occur.
JISHUMI:v10p7247#2/r8.anchor: والمرصاد: مفعال من الرصد المعد لأثر على ارتقاب الوقوع

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p185/r6.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p185/r6.speaker: أبو سنان
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p185/r6.claim: Hell is watchful and requites people for their deeds.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p185/r6.anchor: أحدها : يعني أنها راصدة فجازتهم بأعمالهم , قاله أبو سنان .

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p185/r7.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p185/r7.speaker: الحسن
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p185/r7.claim: A guard is stationed at the Fire, which everyone must cross to reach Paradise; only one with a pass may cross.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p185/r7.anchor: الثاني : أن على النار رصدا , لا يدخل أحد الجنة حتى يجتاز عليه , فمن جاء بجواز جاز

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p185/r8.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p185/r8.speaker: قتادة
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p185/r8.claim: The word is a threat God has made to the disbelievers.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p185/r8.anchor: الثالث : أن المرصاد وعيد أوعد الله به الكفار , قاله قتادة .

TABRISI:78:17-30/r13.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:78:17-30/r13.speaker: الأزهري
TABRISI:78:17-30/r13.claim: Al-Azhari defines mirsad as a place from which an enemy is watched.
TABRISI:78:17-30/r13.anchor: قال الأزهري المرصاد المكان الذي يرصد فيه العدو

THALABI:v10p115/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p115/r3.speaker: author
THALABI:v10p115/r3.claim: Hell lies in wait along the path, which must be crossed before anyone can reach Paradise; Muqatil calls it a prison for transgressors.
THALABI:v10p115/r3.anchor: إن جهنم كانت مرصادا طريقا وممرا فلا سبيل إلى الجنة حتى تقطع النار، وقال مقاتل: محبسا للطاغين

ELMALILI:78:14-30#2/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:78:14-30#2/r1.speaker: author
ELMALILI:78:14-30#2/r1.claim: Mirsad is chiefly a place of watching or ambush, like a hunter's lookout, though it can name the observing instrument or place; its intensive form can figuratively mean a place characterized by constant watching.
ELMALILI:78:14-30#2/r1.anchor: rasad yeri, terassud mahalli mânasına kullanılır ki avcının av gözlediği yer gibi gözetme yeri

ELMALILI:78:14-30#2/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:78:14-30#2/r2.speaker: Ebû Hayyân
ELMALILI:78:14-30#2/r2.claim: Abu Hayyan says relational predicates imply abundance and permanence: Hell is where angels watch to seize rebels whose punishment is decreed.
ELMALILI:78:14-30#2/r2.anchor: Ebû Hayyân der ki: “Nisbet mânasına delâlet eden haberlerin ve sıfatların hepsinde teksir ve lüzum mânası vardır

ELMALILI:78:14-30#2/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:78:14-30#2/r3.speaker: Mukātil
ELMALILI:78:14-30#2/r3.claim: Muqatil glosses Hell as the prison of enemies and the passageway of friends.
ELMALILI:78:14-30#2/r3.anchor: Mukātil demiştir ki düşmanların mahbisi, dostların geçiti

STUDYQURAN:78:21/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:78:21/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:78:21/r1.claim: Hell is where those who rebel against the truth are sent.
STUDYQURAN:78:21/r1.anchor: Hell is the place to which those who rebel against the truth are sent

STUDYQURAN:78:21/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:78:21/r2.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:78:21/r2.claim: Hell ambushes them at death because they were oblivious to the truth in worldly life.
STUDYQURAN:78:21/r2.anchor: It will come upon them like an ambush when they die, because they had been oblivious to the truth in this world

TAB-FULL:v24p20#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p20#2/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v24p20#2/r1.claim: Hell is a watch post lying in wait for those who pass it; it awaits its inhabitants, including those who denied it and the resurrection.
TAB-FULL:v24p20#2/r1.anchor: إن جهنم كانت ذات ارتقاب، ترقب من يجتازها وترصدهم

TAB-FULL:v24p20#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p20#2/r2.speaker: الحسن
TAB-FULL:v24p20#2/r2.claim: Al-Ḥasan warns that watchers stand at Hell’s gate: whoever arrives with a pass gets through, and whoever lacks one is held.
TAB-FULL:v24p20#2/r2.anchor: كان الحسن إذا تلا هذه الآية: {إن جهنم كانت مرصادا} [النبأ: 21] قال: ألا إن على الباب الرصد

TAB-FULL:v24p20#2/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p20#2/r3.speaker: الحسن
TAB-FULL:v24p20#2/r3.claim: Al-Ḥasan says no one enters Paradise without first crossing the Fire.
TAB-FULL:v24p20#2/r3.anchor: عن الحسن، في قوله {إن جهنم كانت مرصادا} [النبأ: 21] قال: «لا يدخل الجنة أحد حتى يجتاز النار»

TAB-FULL:v24p20#2/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p20#2/r4.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v24p20#2/r4.claim: Qatāda says there is no route to Paradise without crossing the Fire.
TAB-FULL:v24p20#2/r4.anchor: عن قتادة، قوله: {إن جهنم كانت مرصادا} [النبأ: 21] يعلمنا أنه لا سبيل إلى الجنة حتى يقطع النار

TAB-FULL:v24p20#2/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p20#2/r5.speaker: سفيان
TAB-FULL:v24p20#2/r5.claim: Sufyān says three bridges span Hell.
TAB-FULL:v24p20#2/r5.anchor: عن سفيان، {إن جهنم كانت مرصادا} [النبأ: 21] قال: عليها ثلاث قناطر

TABATABAI:78:21-23/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:78:21-23/r6.speaker: المفردات
TABATABAI:78:21-23/r6.claim: Al-Mufradāt defines raṣd as readiness to watch, marṣad as a watch post, and mirṣād as a place specifically appointed for watching.
TABATABAI:78:21-23/r6.anchor: قال في المفردات الرصد الاستعداد للترقب

TABATABAI:78:21-23/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:78:21-23/r7.speaker: author
TABATABAI:78:21-23/r7.claim: Calling Hell a watch post signals that people must pass over it, as also stated in the verse that none will fail to come to it.
TABATABAI:78:21-23/r7.anchor: تنبيها على أن عليها مجاز الناس

TABRISI:78:21-24/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:78:21-24/r1.speaker: المبرد
TABRISI:78:21-24/r1.claim: Al-Mubarrid explains that Hell is prepared as a place where its keepers watch for the unbelievers.
TABRISI:78:21-24/r1.anchor: يرصدون به أي هي معدة لهم يرصد بها خزنتها الكفار عن المبرد

TABRISI:78:21-24/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:78:21-24/r2.speaker: مقاتل
TABRISI:78:21-24/r2.claim: Muqātil glosses it as a prison where people are held.
TABRISI:78:21-24/r2.anchor: وقيل: مرصدا محبسا يحبس فيه الناس عن مقاتل

TABRISI:78:21-24/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:78:21-24/r3.speaker: قيل
TABRISI:78:21-24/r3.claim: Another explanation makes it a road set before sinners and their destination; this signals that they cannot escape Hell.
TABRISI:78:21-24/r3.anchor: وقيل: طريقا منصوبا على العاصين فهو موردهم ومنهلهم وهذا إشارة إلى أن جهنم للعصاة على الرصد

BURSEVI:v10p233/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p233/r1.speaker: الراغب
BURSEVI:v10p233/r1.claim: Al-Rāghib defines مرصاد as a place of watching, like مرصد, especially a place set aside for surveillance and waiting.

BURSEVI:v10p233/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p233/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p233/r2.claim: Although the term may be generalized to a path that imprisons enemies and lets saints pass, the author prefers its application to unbelievers and the wretched, since surveillance at such a terrifying place is for punishment.
BURSEVI:v10p233/r2.anchor: والأول أولى لأن الترصد في مثل ذلك المكان الهائل إنما هو للتعذيب

WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p126#4/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p126#4/r1.speaker: الأزهري
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p126#4/r1.claim: Al-Azhari defines a mirṣād as a place where a watcher waits for an enemy, like the place where horses are trained.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p126#4/r1.anchor: قال الأزهري: المرصاد: المكان الذي يرصد الراصد فيه العدو

WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p126#4/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p126#4/r2.speaker: المبرد
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p126#4/r2.claim: Al-Mubarrad calls it a place for watching, meaning Hell is prepared for its occupants.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p126#4/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p126#4/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p126#4/r3.claim: Hell is a station from which its keepers watch the disbelievers.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p126#4/r3.anchor: وجهنم مرصاد يرصد به خزنتها الكفار

WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p126#4/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p126#4/r4.speaker: أبو إسحاق، الحسن
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p126#4/r4.claim: Abu Ishaq says Hell watches unbelievers and those due for punishment; al-Hasan says, by God, it watches them.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p126#4/r4.anchor: قال أبو إسحاق: يرصد أهل الكفر، ومن حق عليه العذاب

WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p126#4/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p126#4/r5.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p126#4/r5.claim: Mirṣād may be an intensive pattern from raṣada, denoting constant watchfulness, like miʿṭār and miʿmār.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p126#4/r5.anchor: وعلى هذا يجوز أن يكون المرصاد مفعالا من الرصد

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:78:21-23/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:78:21-23/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:78:21-23/r1.claim: Hell watches for the disbelievers, who cannot pass beyond it.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:78:21-23/r1.anchor: { إن جهنم كانت مرصادا } ترصد أهل الكفر، فلا يجاوزونها.

QASHANI:78:19-22/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:78:19-22/r3.speaker: author
QASHANI:78:19-22/r3.claim: Hell signifies nature, a boundary where everyone is watched; the blessed must pass over it, after which the God-fearing are rescued, as 19:71–72 says.
QASHANI:78:19-22/r3.anchor: الطبيعة { كانت مرصادا } حدا يرصد فيه كل أحد

QASHANI:78:19-22/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:78:19-22/r4.speaker: الصادق عليه السلام
QASHANI:78:19-22/r4.claim: Asked whether the Ahl al-Bayt also enter Hell, al-Sadiq replied that they had crossed it while it was quiescent.
QASHANI:78:19-22/r4.anchor: وعن الصادق عليه السلام أنه سئل عن الآية فقيل له: أنتم أيضا واردوها؟ فقال: " جزناها وهي خامدة "

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:78:21/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:78:21/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:78:21/r1.claim: After the preceding signs establish resurrection, the passage turns to deniers’ afterlife; Hell is pictured as a warrior lying in wait, warning sinners of danger.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:78:21/r1.anchor: Mülk sûresinin 8. âyetinde canlı bir varlık gibi tasvir edilerek neredeyse öfkesinden çatlayacak duruma geleceği bildirilen cehennem, burada da pusuda düşmanı gözetleyen bir savaşçı gibi tasvir edilmekte

ZAJJAJ:v5p273/r1.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p273/r1.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v5p273/r1.claim: Hell lies in wait, watching over the disbelievers and those against whom punishment is decreed.
ZAJJAJ:v5p273/r1.anchor: يرصد أهل الكفر ومن حق عليه العذاب

ZAJJAJ:v5p273/r2.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p273/r2.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v5p273/r2.claim: Hell nearly bursts with rage, and those sentenced to punishment cannot pass beyond it.
ZAJJAJ:v5p273/r2.anchor: تكاد تميز من الغيظ، فلا يجاوزها من حقت عليه كلمة العذاب

ALUSI-FULL:v30p14/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p14/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p14/r1.claim: This begins the detailed account of judgment after the preceding description of the Day’s terror.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p14/r1.anchor: شروع في تفصيل أحكام الفصل أضيف إليه اليوم أثر بيان هوله

ALUSI-FULL:v30p14/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p14/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p14/r2.claim: Mirṣād can be a place noun, an instrument noun, or an intensive adjective; its apparent sense here is a place of watching and waiting.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p14/r2.anchor: والمرصاد اسم مكان كالمضمار للموضع الذي تضمر فيه الخيل ومفعال يكون كذلك

ALUSI-FULL:v30p14/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p14/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p14/r3.claim: On the apparent reading, Hell is where its keepers wait to punish the transgressors.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p14/r3.anchor: موضع رصد وترقب ترصد فيه خزنة النار ليعذبوهم

ALUSI-FULL:v30p14/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p14/r4.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v30p14/r4.claim: One view says the keepers of Paradise watch there to protect believers from Hell’s heat as they pass over it.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p14/r4.anchor: وقيل ترصد فيه خزنة الجنة المؤمنين ليحرسوهم من فيحها في مجازهم عليها

ALUSI-FULL:v30p14/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p14/r5.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v30p14/r5.claim: Another view has angels watching both groups, protecting one and punishing the other.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p14/r5.anchor: وقيل ترصد الملائكة عليهم السلام الطائفتين لتعذب أحدهما وهي المؤمنة وتعذب الأخرى وهي الكافرة

ALUSI-FULL:v30p14/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p14/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p14/r6.claim: If intensive, the word can describe diligent watching of disbelievers so none escapes, believers so none suffers Hell’s heat, or both groups; attributing this to Hell is figurative or by comparison.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p14/r6.anchor: وجوز أن يكون صيغة مبالغة كمتحار أي مجدة في ترصد الكفرة لئلا يشذ منهم واحد

ALUSI-FULL:v30p14/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p14/r7.speaker: البحر
ALUSI-FULL:v30p14/r7.claim: Al-Baḥr takes mirṣād as a relational adjective meaning that Hell possesses a watch or guard.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p14/r7.anchor: وفي البحر أن مرصادا معنى النسب أي ذات رصد

ALUSI-FULL:v30p14/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p14/r8.speaker: الحسن
ALUSI-FULL:v30p14/r8.claim: Taking mirṣād to mean a road, al-Hasan says everyone must pass Hell before entering Paradise.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p14/r8.anchor: ومن هنا قال الحسن كما أخرج عنه ابن جرير وابن المنذر وعبد بن حميد في الآية لا يدخل الجنة أحد حتى يجتاز النار

ALUSI-FULL:v30p14/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p14/r9.speaker: قتادة
ALUSI-FULL:v30p14/r9.claim: Qatāda likewise warns that there is no way to Paradise until one crosses Hell.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p14/r9.anchor: وقال قتادة كما أخرج هؤلاء عنه أيضا اعلموا أنه لا سبيل إلى الجنة حتى تقطع النار

ALUSI-FULL:v30p14#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p14#2/r5.speaker: أبو عمر
ALUSI-FULL:v30p14#2/r5.claim: Abū ʿAmr, al-Minqari, and Ibn Yaʿmar read the hamza of an as open, supplying a causal preposition: this is for establishing the Hour’s recompense.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p14#2/r5.anchor: وقرأ أبو عمر والمنقري وابن يعمر أن جهنم بفتح الهمزة بتقدير لام جر لتعليل قيام الساعة

ALUSI-FULL:v30p14#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p14#2/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p14#2/r6.claim: Alusi questions the proposed explanation: the phrase about the pious should then also take an open hamza and be coordinated, while the suggestion that each reward independently demands the Hour does not explain establishing recompense itself.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p14#2/r6.anchor: بأنه ينبغي حينئذ أن يكون أن للمتقين أيضا بالفتح ومعطوفا على ما هنا لأنه بكليهما يتم التعليل

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p314/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p314/r2.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p314/r2.claim: Hell is a road and passage; no one can reach Paradise without crossing it.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p314/r2.anchor: طريقا وممرا فلا سبيل لأحد إلى الجنة حتى يقطع النار

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p314/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p314/r3.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p314/r3.claim: Another explanation takes it as prepared for them; arṣadtu something for someone means I prepared it for him.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p314/r3.anchor: وقيل: "كانت مرصادا" أي: معدة لهم، يقال: أرصدت له

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p314/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p314/r4.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p314/r4.claim: A further explanation derives it from watching and waiting: a mirṣād is where a watcher waits for an enemy, so Hell watches the disbelievers.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p314/r4.anchor: وقيل: هو من رصدت الشيء أرصده إذا ترقبته. "والمرصاد" المكان الذي يرصد الراصد فيه العدو.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p314/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p314/r5.speaker: مقسم عن ابن عباس
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p314/r5.claim: Muqsim transmits from Ibn Abbas that a bridge over Hell has seven checkpoints: testimony, prayer, alms, fasting, Hajj, umrah, and wrongs; voluntary worship completes deficient deeds before entry to Paradise.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p314/r5.anchor: وروى مقسم عن ابن عباس: أن على جسر جهنم سبع محابس يسأل العبد عند أولها عن شهادة

BAYDAWI-FULL:78:19-23/r5.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:78:19-23/r5.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:78:19-23/r5.claim: One view makes Hell a place where its keepers lie in wait for unbelievers.
BAYDAWI-FULL:78:19-23/r5.anchor: موضع رصد يرصد فيه خزنة النار الكفار

BAYDAWI-FULL:78:19-23/r6.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:78:19-23/r6.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:78:19-23/r6.claim: Alternatively, keepers of Paradise guard believers from Hell's heat as they pass over it.
BAYDAWI-FULL:78:19-23/r6.anchor: أو خزنة الجنة المؤمنين ليحرسوهم من فيحها في مجازهم عليها

BAYDAWI-FULL:78:19-23/r7.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:78:19-23/r7.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:78:19-23/r7.claim: The word may evoke a place where horses are conditioned, or a vigilant ambush for unbelievers so none escapes, like a fierce attacker.
BAYDAWI-FULL:78:19-23/r7.anchor: كالمضمار فإنه الموضع الذي تضمر فيه الخيل،

BAYDAWI-FULL:78:19-23/r8.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:78:19-23/r8.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:78:19-23/r8.claim: Reading إن with fatḥa makes the clause causal, explaining why the Hour is established.
BAYDAWI-FULL:78:19-23/r8.anchor: وقرىء { أن } بالفتح على التعليل لقيام الساعة

BIQAI-FULL:v8p300/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p300/r8.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p300/r8.claim: Hell is a lookout where its wardens watch for God's enemies and seize them when they arrive.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p300/r8.anchor: أي موضع رصد لأعداء الله ترصدهم فيها خزنة النار

BIQAI-FULL:v8p300/r9.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p300/r9.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p300/r9.claim: Alternatively, its wardens watch for God's friends so Paradise's wardens can rescue them from the Fire when they reach it.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p300/r9.anchor: ولأولياء الله ترصدهم فيها خزنة الجنة لإنجائهم من النار عند ورودها

BIQAI-FULL:v8p300/r10.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p300/r10.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p300/r10.claim: Alternatively, Hell itself is an intensely watchful sentry, personified as an inescapable collector of all unbelievers, like an intensive noun for one who stabs repeatedly.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p300/r10.anchor: أوهي راصدة بليغة الرصد للكفار حتى صارت مجسدة من الرصد لتجمع أصحابها فلا يفوت منهم واحد

BIQAI-FULL:v8p300/r11.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p300/r11.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p300/r11.claim: The author describes seven checkpoints: confession, prayer, alms, fasting, pilgrimage, minor pilgrimage, and wrongs; if wrongs remain, optional worship completes one's deeds before the person proceeds to Paradise.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p300/r11.anchor: مجالس يسأل عند أولها عن شهادة أن لا إله إلا الله , فإن جاء بها تامة

BIQAI-FULL:v8p300/r12.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p300/r12.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p300/r12.claim: Because averting harm takes priority over gaining benefit, the fearful destination is presented first.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p300/r12.anchor: ولما كان درء المفاسد أولى من جلب المصالح , قدم ذكر المخوف

DURR-FULL:v8p393/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p393/r4.speaker: أبو الجوزاء
DURR-FULL:v8p393/r4.anchor: عن أبي الجوزاء في قوله: {إن جهنم كانت مرصادا} قال: صارت

DURR-FULL:v8p393/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p393/r5.speaker: الحسن
DURR-FULL:v8p393/r5.claim: Al-Hasan says no one enters Paradise without first crossing the Fire.
DURR-FULL:v8p393/r5.anchor: عن الحسن في قوله: {إن جهنم كانت مرصادا} قال: لا يدخل الجنة أحد حتى يجتاز النار

DURR-FULL:v8p393/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p393/r6.speaker: سفيان
DURR-FULL:v8p393/r6.claim: Sufyan describes three bridges over Hell that everyone must cross before entering Paradise.
DURR-FULL:v8p393/r6.anchor: عن سفيان {إن جهنم كانت مرصادا} قال: عليهم ثلاث قناطر لا يدخل الجنة أحد حتى يجتاز النار

DURR-FULL:v8p394/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p394/r1.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v8p394/r1.claim: Qatadah says there is no route to Paradise until people cross the Fire, linking it with 19:71.
DURR-FULL:v8p394/r1.anchor: عن قتادة {إن جهنم كانت مرصادا} قال: تعلموا أنه لا سبيل إلى الجنة حتى تقطع النار

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p33/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p33/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p33/r3.claim: One construction makes this a second predicate of the initial inna in 78:17, estimating an omitted in it on that day, since a watch-post and a fixed appointment both mark a time for punishing the rebellious.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p33/r3.anchor: يجوز أن تكون جملة { إن جهنم كانت مرصادا } في موضع خبر ثان ل { إن } من قوله

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p33/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p33/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p33/r4.claim: An inna inside the predicate adds emphasis to the emphasis already supplied by inna before the Day of Decision, a construction also found in Jarir's line and 22:17.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p33/r4.anchor: ودخول حرف ( إن ) في خبر ( إن ) يفيد تأكيدا على التأكيد الذي أفاده حرف التأكيد

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p33/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p33/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p33/r5.claim: On this construction the clause completes what the audience was told about the day when they would come in companies.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p33/r5.anchor: وتكون الجملة من تمام ما خوطبوا به بقوله : يوم ينفخ في الصور فتأتون أفواجا

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p33/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p33/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p33/r7.claim: The passage starts with Hell because its setting is a threat to those who deny resurrection, and the ordering of the following statements supports this.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p33/r7.anchor: وابتدىء بذكر جهنم لأن المقام مقام تهديد إذ ابتدئت السورة بذكر تكذيب المشركين بالبعث

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p33/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p33/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p33/r8.claim: Alternatively, the sentence can independently answer the audience's implied question about what follows the horrors of the Day of Decision; in this reading al-taghin is not a marked departure from expected wording.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p33/r8.anchor: ويجوز أن تكون مستأنفة استئنافا بيانيا عن جملة { إن يوم الفصل كان ميقاتا }

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p35/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p35/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p35/r1.claim: Jahannam names the abode of afterlife punishment; it may be a borrowed, declined name from Hebrew or another Semitic language.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p35/r1.anchor: وجهنم : اسم لدار العذاب في الآخرة . قيل : وهو اسم معرب فلعله معرب عن العبرانية

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p35/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p35/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p35/r2.claim: Mirsad is a place of watching or surveillance, on a pattern commonly used for an instrument or a place of an action.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p35/r2.anchor: والمرصاد : مكان الرصد ، أي الرقابة ، وهو بوزن مفعال الذي غلب في اسم آلة الفعل

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p35/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p35/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p35/r3.claim: Hell is a place where its appointed keepers watch for those sent there from among the rebellious, as guards at an outpost watch for an enemy.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p35/r3.anchor: والمعنى : أن جهنم موضع يرصد منه الموكلون بها ، ويترقبون من يزجى إليها من أهل الطغيان

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p35/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p35/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p35/r4.claim: Mirsad may instead be a verbal noun meaning surveillance; predicating it of Hell intensifies the image, as if Hell itself were the source of watching and lets none destined for it escape.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p35/r4.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون مرصاد مصدرا على وزن المفعال ، أي رصدا . والإخبار به عن جهنم للمبالغة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p35/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p35/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p35/r5.claim: Alternatively, mirsad is an intensive watcher; Hell is metaphorically described as a relentless male guard, so the feminine ending is omitted.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p35/r5.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون مرصاد زنة مبالغة للراصد الشديد الرصد مثل صفة مغيار ومعطار

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p35/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p35/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p35/r6.claim: The omitted complement of mirsad is supplied by maʾaban: it is a watch-post for the rebellious. This is best because the short verse cola allow a pause after mirsad.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p35/r6.anchor: والتقدير : مرصادا للطاغين ، وهذا أحسن لأن قرائن السورة قصار فيحسن الوقف عند { مرصادا }

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p35/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p35/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p35/r7.claim: Other parses attach lil-taghin to mirsad and infer the complement of maʾaban, or let lil-taghin depend on both terms; neither alternative creates a semantic obstacle.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p35/r7.anchor: ولك أن تجعل { للطاغين } متعلقا ب { مرصادا } وتجعل متعلق { مئابا } مقدرا دل عليه { للطاغين }

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p35/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p35/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p35/r8.claim: Kana signals that Hell's role as a watch-post was preordained, as the Day of Decision was appointed; this hints at God's eternal preparation of punishment.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p35/r8.anchor: وأقحم { كانت } دون أن يقال : إن جهنم مرصاد للدلالة على أن جعلها مرصادا أمر مقدر لها

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p110/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p110/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p110/r1.claim: Sentence placement can signal a cause, correction, answer, allusion, or other relation to what precedes and follows; Quranic length allows multiple such relations unlike the limited aims of Arab poetry and oratory.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p110/r1.anchor: العلة لكلام قبلها ، أو في موقع الاستدراك ، أو في موقع جواب سؤال ، أو في موقع تعريض أو نحوه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p110/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p110/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p110/r3.claim: Opening with Hell explains the later word mafazan as Paradise, a place of triumph for the God-fearing.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p110/r3.anchor: فكان للابتداء بذكر جهنم ما يفسر المفاز في قوله ) إن للمتقين مفازا ( أنه الجنة لأن الجنة مكان فوز

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p110/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p110/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p110/r6.claim: These several readings depend on the exact order of Hell, mafazan, the overflowing cup, and the no-speech clause; the sequence makes meanings available that a different order would not.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p110/r6.anchor: وهذه المعاني لا يتأتى جميعها إلا بجمل كثيرة لو لم يقدم ذكر جهنم ولم يعقب بكلمة ) مفازا ( . ولم يؤخر ) وكأسا دهاقا (

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p110/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p110/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p110/r7.claim: Rhetorical choices must be explained by the occasion and audience of revelation; reading only the local words can make interpreters force strained explanations.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p110/r7.anchor: ذلك لأنه لم يلتفت إلا إلى مواقع ألفاظ الآية ، في حال أن مقتضياتها في الواقع منوطة بالمقامات التي نزلت فيها الآية

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p7#6/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p7#6/r1.speaker: المبرد
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p7#6/r1.claim: Al-Mubarrad explains the word as an observation post prepared for the unbelievers, watched by its keepers.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p7#6/r1.anchor: قال المبرد مرصادا يرصدون به أي هو معد لهم يرصد بها خزنتها الكفار

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p7#6/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p7#6/r2.speaker: الأزهري
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p7#6/r2.claim: Al-Azharī defines a mirṣād as a place where a watcher lies in wait for an enemy.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p7#6/r2.anchor: وقال الأزهري المرصاد المكان الذي يرصد فيه الراصد العدو

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p305/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p305/r3.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p305/r3.claim: Hell is lying in wait, prepared for its inhabitants.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p305/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p305/r6.speaker: الحسن وقتادة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p305/r6.claim: Al-Hasan and Qatada say no one enters Paradise without crossing the Fire: one with a pass is saved, while the rest are detained.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p305/r6.anchor: وقال الحسن، وقتادة في قوله: {إن جهنم كانت مرصادا} يعني: أنه لا يدخل أحد الجنة حتى يجتاز بالنار،

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p305/r7.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p305/r7.speaker: سفيان الثوري
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p305/r7.claim: Sufyan al-Thawri says three crossing bridges are set over the Fire.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p305/r7.anchor: وقال سفيان الثوري: عليها ثلاث قناطر.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p688#2/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p688#2/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p688#2/r1.claim: Al-mirṣād is a place or boundary where watching and surveillance take place.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p688#2/r1.anchor: المرصاد : الحد الذي يكون فيه الرصد

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p688#2/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p688#2/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p688#2/r2.claim: Hell is the limit and destination of the tyrants, where they are watched for punishment.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p688#2/r2.anchor: أن جهنم هي حد الطاغين الذي يرصدون فيه للعذاب وهي مآبهم

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p688#2/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p688#2/r3.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p688#2/r3.claim: Another possible sense is that angels await the people of Paradise at Hell, which they cross, while it remains the tyrants’ destination.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p688#2/r3.anchor: أو هي مرصاد لأهل الجنة ترصدهم الملائكة الذين يستقبلونهم عندها

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p688#2/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p688#2/r4.speaker: الحسن وقتادة
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p688#2/r4.claim: Hasan and Qatada likewise describe it as a route and passage for the people of Paradise.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p688#2/r4.anchor: وعن الحسن وقتادة نحوه ، قالا : طريقا وممرا لأهل الجنة

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p688#2/r5.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p688#2/r5.speaker: ابن يعمر
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p688#2/r5.claim: Ibn Yaʿmur reads the hamza of inna with fatḥa, making Hell’s being an ambush the reason for establishing the Hour and recompense.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p688#2/r5.anchor: وقرأ ابن يعمر ( أن جهنم ) بفتح الهمزة على تعليل قيام الساعة

MUQATIL:78:20-29/r3.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:78:20-29/r3.speaker: author
MUQATIL:78:20-29/r3.claim: The transgressors are unbelievers, and their return is to Hell; the verse was revealed concerning al-Walid ibn al-Mughira.
MUQATIL:78:20-29/r3.anchor: يعني الكافرين { مآبا } [آية: 22] يعني المشركين مرجعا إليها

NASAFI-FULL:v4p311#3/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p311#3/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p311#3/r1.claim: Hell is a path all creatures cross: believers pass over it, while disbelievers enter it.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p311#3/r1.anchor: طريقا عليه ممر الخلق فالمؤمن يمر عليها والكافر يدخلها

NASAFI-FULL:v4p311#3/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p311#3/r2.speaker: قيل
NASAFI-FULL:v4p311#3/r2.claim: Another view takes it as a boundary where tyrants are watched for punishment, and as their destination.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p311#3/r2.anchor: وقيل المرصاد الحد الذي يكون فيه الرصد أي هي حد الطاغين الذين يرصدون فيه للعذاب وهي مآبهم

NASAFI-FULL:v4p311#3/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p311#3/r3.speaker: قيل
NASAFI-FULL:v4p311#3/r3.claim: A further view says Hell watches for the people of Paradise, whom the angels receive there because they must cross it.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p311#3/r3.anchor: أو هي مرصاد لأهل الجنة ترصدهم الملائكة الذين يستقبلونهم عندها لأن مجازهم عليها

QURTUBI-FULL:78:21-25/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:78:21-25/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:78:21-25/r1.claim: Marṣād is mifaʿāl from raṣad, something lying ahead.
QURTUBI-FULL:78:21-25/r1.anchor: مفعال من الرصد والرصد: كل شيء كان أمامك

QURTUBI-FULL:78:21-25/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:78:21-25/r2.speaker: الحسن
QURTUBI-FULL:78:21-25/r2.claim: Al-Hasan describes a checkpoint at Hell: none reaches Paradise without crossing; a person with a pass crosses and one without it is detained.
QURTUBI-FULL:78:21-25/r2.anchor: قال الحسن: إن على النار رصدا، لا يدخل أحد الجنة

QURTUBI-FULL:78:21-25/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:78:21-25/r3.speaker: سفيان
QURTUBI-FULL:78:21-25/r3.claim: Sufyan says there are three bridges over Hell.
QURTUBI-FULL:78:21-25/r3.anchor: وعن سفيان رضي الله عنه قال: عليها ثلاث قناطر

QURTUBI-FULL:78:21-25/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:78:21-25/r4.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI-FULL:78:21-25/r4.claim: Another parsing makes marṣād mean possessing watchers who watch passersby.
QURTUBI-FULL:78:21-25/r4.anchor: وقيل «مرصادا» ذات أرصاد على النسب، أي ترصد من يمر بها

QURTUBI-FULL:78:21-25/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:78:21-25/r5.speaker: مقاتل
QURTUBI-FULL:78:21-25/r5.claim: Muqatil glosses marṣād as a prison.

QURTUBI-FULL:78:21-25/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:78:21-25/r6.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI-FULL:78:21-25/r6.claim: Another view calls it a road or passage, so reaching Paradise requires crossing Hell.
QURTUBI-FULL:78:21-25/r6.anchor: وقيل: طريقا وممرا، فلا سبيل إلى الجنة

QURTUBI-FULL:78:21-25/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:78:21-25/r7.speaker: الصحاح
QURTUBI-FULL:78:21-25/r7.claim: Al-Ṣiḥāḥ records that marṣād means a road.

QURTUBI-FULL:78:21-25/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:78:21-25/r8.speaker: القشيري
QURTUBI-FULL:78:21-25/r8.claim: Al-Qushayri defines a marṣād as a place for watching an enemy, like a place for training horses; angels watch unbelievers until they descend to Hell.
QURTUBI-FULL:78:21-25/r8.anchor: وذكر القشيري: أن المرصاد المكان الذي يرصد فيه الواحد العدو

QURTUBI-FULL:78:21-25/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:78:21-25/r9.speaker: أبو سنان
QURTUBI-FULL:78:21-25/r9.claim: Al-Mawardi cites Abu Sinan: marṣād means a watcher who repays people according to their deeds.
QURTUBI-FULL:78:21-25/r9.anchor: عن أبي سنان أنها بمعنى راصدة، تجازيهم بأفعالهم

QURTUBI-FULL:78:21-25/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:78:21-25/r10.speaker: الأصمعي
QURTUBI-FULL:78:21-25/r10.claim: Al-Aṣmaʿi and al-Kisaʾi distinguish watching from preparing something; tarassud is waiting and marṣad is a watch post.

QURTUBI-FULL:78:21-25/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:78:21-25/r11.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:78:21-25/r11.claim: Qurtubi concludes Hell is prepared and waiting for those who come to it.

QURTUBI-FULL:78:21-25/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:78:21-25/r12.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:78:21-25/r12.claim: Mifaʿāl is an intensive pattern, suggesting Hell’s frequent waiting for unbelievers.
QURTUBI-FULL:78:21-25/r12.anchor: والمرصاد مفعال من أبنية المبالغة كالمعطار والمغيار
